revenue_model.description: The company sells hardware products such as iPhone, Mac, iPad, and wearables primarily to consumers and businesses. It also sells services including iCloud, Siri, and Maps, and earns commissions from third-party applications sold through its App Store.
revenue_model.quote: The Company has identified the performance obligations regularly included in arrangements involving the sale of iPhone, Mac and iPad. The first material performance obligation, which represents the substantial portion of the allocated sales price, is the hardware and bundled software delivered at the time of sale. The second material performance obligation is the right to receive certain product-related bundled services, which include iCloud®, Siri® and Maps. ... For third-party applications sold through the App Store, the Company does not obtain control of the product before transferring it to the customer. Therefore, the Company accounts for all third-party application–related sales on a net basis by recognizing in Services net sales only the commission it retains.

business_structure.description: Apple Inc. is a publicly listed company organized as an Inc. It manages its business primarily on a geographic basis with reportable segments including Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan, and Rest of Asia Pacific.
business_structure.quote: The Company’s reportable segments consist of the Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan and Rest of Asia Pacific. ... The Company manages its business primarily on a geographic basis. The Company’s CEO is its CODM.
